newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP steel workers to strike for day.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP steel workers to strike for day.

text.p: A meeting of unions voted on Monday for a nationwide strike of all Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's (BHP) steelworkers for 24 hours on Thursday, May 15.

"At this stage, it is confined to steel and associated workers but if necessary we will meet and discuss with workers in other parts of the organisation," the Australian Council of Trade Union (ACTU) president Jennie George told reporters.
George said the action against BHP would not stop BHP exports at this stage and no mention was made of energy workers.
The strike action against BHP follows its decision announced last week to end steel making at Newcastle in New South Wales.
ACTU officials met today with the Australian Workers Union, as well as some other unions covering other BHP workers.
George said urgent meetings would be sought within a month of the stop work meeting with BHP and Prime Minister John Howard.
The meetings would be conducted by the ACTU and the Trades and Labour Council.
George said unions would also be holding public meetings in Newcastle to protest against BHP's decision.
BHP announced last week a wide-ranging restructure of its steel division, including the closure of its Newcastle steel-making operations and the associated laying off of 2,500 workers.
Newcastle's rod and bar mills would be retained and developed into the centre for BHP's rod, bar and wire business.
BHP's 3,000 Newcastle workers went on a 24 hour strike last Friday.
BHP shares were nine cents firmer at A$18.13 at 2.50 p.m. (0450 GMT).
